newsitem.title: USA: NHL-VISITING RED WINGS BEAT FLYERS IN STANLEY CUP FINALS OPENER.
newsitem.headline: NHL-VISITING RED WINGS BEAT FLYERS IN STANLEY CUP FINALS OPENER.

text.p: The Detroit Red Wings, getting first-period goals from grinders Kirk Maltby and Joey Kocur, stunned the host Philadelphia Flyers 4-2 Saturday in the opening game of the Stanley Cup finals.

Sharp-shooters Sergei Fedorov and Steve Yzerman also scored for the Red Wings, while defenceman Larry Murphy chipped in with two key assists as Detroit took a one game to none lead in the best-of-seven series.
Game 2 will be played in Philadelphia on Tuesday before the series shifts to Detrot for the next two games.
The Flyers, who finished third in the Eastern Conference of the National Hockey League, got goals from Rod Brind'Amour and John Leclair with their captain Eric Lindros assisting on both tallies.

Detroit is hoping to end a 42-year championship drought. Victory in Game 1 gives the Red Wings reason for hope -- the team that has won the Stanley Cup opener has gone on to win the Cup 46 times in the last 58 years.

The Wings, who upset the defending champion Colorado Avalanche to reach the finals, shocked the sold out Core States Centre crowd of 20,291, by beating Flyers goalie Ron Hextall just 6:38 into the game.
Maltby, killing a penalty to Detroit's Tomas Sandstrom, poked the puck away from Lindros and broke in two-on-none with Kris Draper on Hextall and beat the Flyer netminder with a 10-footer.
Philadelphia bounced back to tie the game less than a minute later with a power play goal at 7:37 as Brind'Amour jammed the puck past Detroit goalie Mike Vernon from in close.
The game turned at 15:56 when Detroit tough guy Joey Kocur stole from the puck at the Philadelphia blue line from Kjell Samuelsson and walked in alone and faked out Hextall to put Detroit ahead 2-1.
Each team scored once in the second period, with the skilled Russian Fedorov cashing in a two-on-one break with Murphy with a straight on 28-footer.
The Flyers goal came from Leclair, who beat Vernon with a blast through the goalie's legs at 17:11.

The third period started with Detroit ahead by just one goal at 3-2, but Yzerman gave the Wings some cushion with a 55-foot blast from just inside the Flyers zone that handcuffed the Philadelphia netminder.
The Red Wings, who have been in two of the last three finals, outshot Philadelphia 30-28.
